mainTopic: Proof of adulthood from childbirth; the rules of צרת ערוה (צרת צרה, divorce of the ערוה, מיאון); and the six stricter עריות
overview: This amud covers several short topics. First, רב זביד explains that a girl who gave birth must already have the סימנים of adulthood. We cannot simply check her, because the hairs may have fallen out, especially from צער לידה. Next, the גמרא asks for the source that even a צרת צרה is exempt from יבום. רב יהודה learns it from the extra ר in לצרור, and רב אשי says it is simple סברא. Then the גמרא sets our משנה against a משנה about three brothers, which seems to require that the ערוה be divorced before the צרה was married. רבי ירמיה says two תנאים disagree, while רבא says it is one תנא teaching an easier case and a harder case. The גמרא then asks why a minor ערוה cannot do מיאון after the death to free her צרה, and explains that a צרת ערוה is set by how things looked at the moment of נפילה. Finally, a new משנה lists six stricter עריות whose צרות are permitted, and records that בית שמאי permit צרות to the brothers while בית הלל forbid them.

steps.title: רב זביד: Children come only with signs of adulthood
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד says that if a girl gave birth, she must already have the סימנים of adulthood.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב זביד said: There are no children without signs of adulthood.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד gives his reason why a girl who has given birth is treated as an adult: anyone who can have children must already have the physical signs of adulthood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being able to give birth shows that her body has matured. So רב זביד treats the birth itself as evidence that she has סימנים, even if nobody has seen them.

phrases.english: And Rav Zevid said:
There are no children without signs of adulthood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another explanation, alongside earlier views, for why a girl who gave birth counts as an adult.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Giving birth proves that the girl has the סימנים of adulthood.

steps.title: Why not just check her?
steps.stepSummary: If she must have the signs, we could simply examine her instead of relying on an assumption.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us examine her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב זביד: if the signs must be there, why rely on an assumption? We could simply look.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A direct check would be more certain than a conclusion drawn from the birth. So why do we need רב זביד's rule at all?

phrases.english: But let us examine her!
phrases.notes: Check whether the hairs are there, instead of assuming they are.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for רב זביד's assumption.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב זביד's reliance on the birth as proof
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A physical check is possible, so no assumption should be needed.

steps.title: The hairs may have fallen out
steps.stepSummary: Checking would not settle it, because the hairs might have fallen out.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are concerned that perhaps they fell out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: if we check and find no hairs, that proves nothing, because they may have been there and fallen out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A check can prove she is an adult if hairs are found. But if none are found, it cannot prove she is not. So the birth remains the reliable sign.

phrases.english: We are concerned that perhaps they fell out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the proposed check is not conclusive
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Checking for hairs would settle the question.
steps.terutzMaskana: If no hairs are found, they may have fallen out, so the check cannot rule out adulthood.

steps.title: That only works for one opinion
steps.stepSummary: The answer fits the view that we worry signs fall out, but not the view that we don't.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well according to the one who says we are concerned. But according to the one who says we are not concerned, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that there is a מחלוקת about whether we worry that hairs fell out. The last answer only works for one side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some hold that if hairs had been there, they would still be found. According to them, checking would work, so the question of step 2 comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says

phrases.english: This works well according to the one who says we are concerned.
phrases.notes: Concerned, that is, that the hairs may have fallen out.

phrases.english: But according to the one who says we are not concerned —
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the answer of step 3 to one opinion and renews the challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the hairs may have fallen out
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Some hold we do not worry about hairs falling out. According to them, checking should work.

steps.title: Childbirth pain is a special reason to worry
steps.stepSummary: Even those who usually don't worry agree that the pain of birth can make the hairs fall out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even according to the one who says we are not concerned, because of the pain of childbirth we are concerned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that childbirth is a special case. The strain of giving birth can cause the hairs to fall out, so everyone agrees to worry here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general opinion not to worry applies to ordinary situations. צער לידה is an unusual cause, so checking her is not conclusive according to any view.
steps.whatToRemember: A girl who gave birth is treated as an adult because there are no children without סימנים. We cannot simply check her, because the hairs may have fallen out, especially from צער לידה.

phrases.english: Even according to the one who says we are not concerned —
because of the pain of childbirth, we are concerned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes a special case where everyone agrees
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Those who do not worry about falling hairs would allow a check here.
steps.terutzMaskana: Childbirth is unusual, so even they worry that the hairs fell out.

steps.title: Where do we learn that a rival's rival is exempt?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about exempting צרות and asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do they exempt their rival wives, etc. From where are these matters derived?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה, which says the ערוה exempts her צרה and even the צרה of that צרה. It asks where this comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is mainly about the further level, the צרת צרה. She was never a co-wife of the ערוה herself, only of the צרה, so why should she be exempt?

keyTerms.meaning: Their rival wives (other wives of the same husband)
From where are these matters derived?

phrases.english: How do they exempt their rival wives, etc.
From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section that returns to the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that a צרה, and even a צרת צרה, is exempt.

steps.title: רב יהודה: The extra letter in לצרור
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה learns from the doubled ר in לצרור that the תורה includes many levels of צרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: Because the verse says לצרור (to be a rival), the תורה included many rival wives.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers from a פסוק. The word לצרור has an extra ר, which teaches that the exemption reaches more than one level of צרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה could have written the shorter לצור. The extra letter adds more צרות, so the צרת צרה is included too.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said: As the verse says:
"To be a rival" —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:18. The word has two ר's where one would have been enough.

phrases.english: the Torah included many rival wives.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6 from a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra ר in לצרור includes many levels of צרות, including the צרת צרה.

steps.title: רב אשי: It's simple logic
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says no פסוק is needed: a צרת צרה stands in the place of the ערוה, just like a צרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: It is logic. Why is a rival wife forbidden? Because she stands in the place of a forbidden relative. A rival of a rival also stands in the place of a forbidden relative.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a different answer. He says the rule comes from סברא, not from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A צרה is forbidden because she takes on the status of the ערוה. Once she has that status, her own צרה is in the same position, so the same rule passes on to her.

keyTerms.meaning: The rival wife of a rival wife

steps.whatToRemember: There are two sources for exempting a צרת צרה: רב יהודה learns it from the extra ר in לצרור, and רב אשי learns it from סברא, since she too stands in the place of the ערוה.
steps.confusionAlert: Both opinions agree on the law. They only disagree about where it comes from, a פסוק or logic.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: It is logic:
A rival wife, why is she forbidden?
Because she stands in the place of a forbidden relative.
A rival of a rival also
stands in the place of a forbidden relative.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 6, from logic instead of a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A צרת צרה stands in the place of the ערוה just as the צרה does, so she is exempt by logic.

steps.title: Our משנה applies even if he married first and divorced later
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line about the ערוה dying or being divorced, and notes that this holds even if the brother married the צרה first and only afterward divorced the ערוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'How so? If they died, etc.' This is true even if he married the other wife first and only in the end divorced the ערוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes our משנה and points out how wide its rule is: even if the two women were once married to him together, the צרה is permitted once the ערוה is gone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives a general rule: if the ערוה died or was divorced, her צרה is permitted. Because the rule is general, the גמרא reads it to cover the case where the two women were צרות to each other for a while. This sets up the contradiction in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? The משנה's opening word for explaining its rule
He married (here, he took the second wife)

phrases.english: How so? If they died, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes our משנה: if the ערוה died, did מיאון, or was divorced, her צרות are permitted.

phrases.english: And even if he married and in the end divorced.
phrases.notes: He married the צרה while still married to the ערוה, and only later divorced the ערוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיצַד אִם מֵתוּ הֵן כּוּ׳. וַאֲפִילּוּ כָּנַס וּלְבַסּוֹף גֵּירַשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic on the משנה's case of a divorced ערוה, after the source discussion about צרת צרה in steps 6-8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Divorcing the ערוה permits her צרה even if the brother married the צרה first and divorced the ערוה later.

steps.title: Bringing a different משנה about three brothers and two sisters
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה about three brothers, two of them married to sisters, where the brother divorced the sister before taking the יבמה. That משנה says this is the case where the צרות are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Contrast this with another משנה: Three brothers. Two are married to two sisters, and one is married to an unrelated woman. One of the sisters' husbands divorced his wife. Then the brother married to the unrelated woman died, and the divorcing brother married her through יבום and then died. This is the case where they said: if they died or were divorced, their צרות are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a contradiction by quoting another משנה. The next step will point out what this משנה implies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this משנה, the brother divorced his wife (the sister) first and only then married the יבמה. So when he died, the יבמה had never been a צרה of the sister. The משנה says that this is the case where 'their צרות are permitted.'

keyTerms.meaning: And contrast it with: introduces a source that seems to contradict
An unrelated woman (not a gentile here)

steps.confusionAlert: נׇכְרִית here does not mean a non-Jewish woman. It means a woman who is not related to the other brothers' wives.

phrases.english: And contrast it with:
Three brothers,
two of them married to two sisters,
and one married to an unrelated woman.
One of the sisters' husbands divorced his wife,
and the one married to the unrelated woman died,
and the one who divorced married her, and died.
This is the case about which they said:
that if they died or were divorced,
their rival wives are permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second משנה to set against the reading of our משנה in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading in step 9 that the צרה is permitted even if he married her before divorcing the ערוה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup: the other משנה describes the permitted case as one where the divorce came first.

steps.title: The other משנה implies that marrying first and divorcing later does not work
steps.stepSummary: From the other משנה, the גמרא infers that the צרה is permitted only because the divorce came before the marriage. If he married first and divorced later, she would not be permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason she is permitted is that he divorced first and married afterward. But if he married first and divorced afterward, she would not be permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its challenge. The other משנה implies the exact opposite of what we learned from our משנה in step 9.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה suggested that the order makes no difference. The other משנה stressed that the divorce came first, which implies that the order does matter. If she was ever a צרה of the ערוה, even for a short time, she stays forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason is: introduces a precise reading of a source
No; it would not be so

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the order of events. Divorce first and then marriage means she was never a צרה. Marriage first and then divorce means she was a צרה for a while.

phrases.english: The reason is that he divorced and afterward married;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל כָּנַס וְאַחַר כָּךְ גֵּירַשׁ — לָא!
phrases.english: but if he married and afterward divorced, no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the contradicting inference from the משנה quoted in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 9's reading that the order of marriage and divorce does not matter.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The other משנה permits the צרה only when the divorce came first. That implies she stays forbidden if she was ever a צרה, which contradicts our משנה.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: the two משניות come from different תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה admits that the two משניות really disagree and come from different תנאים. The תנא of our משנה holds that the moment of death is what decides.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: It is broken! Whoever taught this one did not teach that one. This תנא holds that death is what makes her fall to the brother.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה answers the contradiction. He does not try to make the two משניות agree. He says each one follows a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה's תנא looks only at the moment the brother dies. If she is not a צרה of a ערוה at that moment, she is permitted, even if she was a צרה earlier. The next step explains the other תנא's view.

keyTerms.term: מִי שֶׁשָּׁנָה זוֹ לֹא שָׁנָה זוֹ
keyTerms.meaning: Whoever taught this did not teach that, meaning different תנאים
A sage of the משנה period
Death makes her fall (to יבום); the moment of death decides

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the main idea of the סוגיא: which moment counts, the time of death or some earlier time?

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
It is broken!
phrases.notes: He means the two משניות really do clash, and there is no way to make them fit together.

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁשָּׁנָה זוֹ לֹא שָׁנָה זוֹ.
phrases.english: Whoever taught this one did not teach that one.
This תנא holds
death makes her fall,
phrases.notes: What counts is her status at the moment the brother dies. Then she is either exempt or comes before the יבם.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: תַּבְרָא, מִי שֶׁשָּׁנָה זוֹ לֹא שָׁנָה זוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in steps 10-11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the sources between different תנאים (תברא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed both משניות follow one view, so they would have to agree about the order of marriage and divorce.
steps.terutzMaskana: They follow two different תנאים. Our משנה's תנא holds that the moment of death decides, so earlier צרה status does not matter.

steps.title: The other תנא looks at the moment of the first marriage
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה finishes his answer. The תנא of the three-brothers משנה holds that the first marriage decides the status.
steps.simpleTranslation: And that תנא holds that the first marriage is what makes her fall to the יבם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבי ירמיה's answer by giving the view of the second תנא, the one in the משנה about three brothers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our תנא looks at the moment of the husband's death. The other תנא looks back to the moment the brother married the צרה. If the ערוה was still married to him at that moment, even for a short time, the צרה became a צרת ערוה and stays forbidden. So she is permitted only if the divorce came before the marriage.

keyTerms.meaning: the first marriage, the original marriage to the dead brother
make her fall, meaning they bring her to the יבם for יבום or חליצה

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי ירמיה, the two משניות disagree. One looks at the time of death, and the other looks at the time of the first marriage.

phrases.english: And that תנא holds:
phrases.notes: "That תנא" is the one who taught the משנה about the three brothers from step 10.

phrases.english: the first marriage is what makes her fall to the יבם.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of רבי ירמיה's answer: the view of the other תנא
steps.terutzResolutionType: מחלוקת תנאים, a real disagreement between two תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both משניות seemed to follow one view, so they seemed to contradict each other
steps.terutzMaskana: The other תנא decides by the first marriage, so a divorce after he married the צרה is too late

steps.title: רבא: one תנא, teaching an easier case and a harder case
steps.stepSummary: רבא says both משניות come from the same תנא. The three-brothers משנה just teaches the obvious case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Really it is one תנא. He teaches in the style of "this, and there is no need to say that."
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer to the contradiction. There is no disagreement at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה teaches the bigger חידוש: the צרה is permitted even if he married her first and divorced the ערוה later. The three-brothers משנה teaches the easier case, where he divorced first, and there she is surely permitted. The other משנה never meant that only that case works.

keyTerms.meaning: really, actually, a word that brings back an earlier assumption
"this, and there is no need to say that": teaching one case when another case is even more obvious

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read the three-brothers משנה as saying "only if he divorced first." רבא says it is just giving the simple case, and it does not rule out the harder one.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי ירמיה: two תנאים who disagree. רבא: one תנא, and the two משניות give a harder case and an easier case.

phrases.english: רבא said:
Really, it is one תנא,

phrases.aramaic: וְזוֹ וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר זוֹ קָתָנֵי.
phrases.english: and he teaches "this, and there is no need to say that."
phrases.notes: "This" is our harder case, where he married first and divorced later. "That" is the obvious case, where he divorced first.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם חַד תַּנָּא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different answer to the same contradiction, instead of רבי ירמיה's two-תנאים answer
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the משנה's style: "this, and there is no need to say that"
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The three-brothers משנה seemed to mean that the צרה is permitted only when the divorce came first
steps.terutzMaskana: Both משניות agree. The other משנה just picked the simpler case.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about a ערוה who could do מיאון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a new line from our משנה about a ערוה who is a minor and could have done מיאון.
steps.simpleTranslation: And any of them who could do מיאון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה to set up its next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules that if the ערוה was a minor who could have refused her husband but did not, her צרה does חליצה and not יבום. The גמרא is about to ask why that should be.

keyTerms.meaning: to do מיאון: a minor girl, married off by her mother or brothers, refuses the marriage and undoes it
refusal by a minor girl of a marriage made by the rabbis' rules

phrases.english: And any of them who could do מיאון.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ערוה who could have done מיאון but did not: her צרה does חליצה and does not do יבום

steps.title: Why can't she refuse now and free her צרה for יבום?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the minor ערוה can't do מיאון now, after the death, so that her צרה could do יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let her do מיאון now, and let the צרה do יבום!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's ruling. If she does מיאון now, it looks like the ערוה was never married to him, so the צרה should not be a צרת ערוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מיאון undoes her marriage to the dead brother. If that worked after his death, the צרה would not be the צרה of a ערוה, and she could do יבום. The משנה does not allow this, and the גמרא wants to know why.

phrases.english: Let her do מיאון now,
phrases.notes: "She" here is the minor ערוה, after the husband has already died.

phrases.english: and let her do יבום!
phrases.notes: This "her" is the צרה, who would then be free to do יבום.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling just quoted
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the צרה can only do חליצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מיאון after the death could undo the ערוה's marriage, and then the צרה would not be a צרת ערוה

steps.title: This seems to support רבי אושעיא: no מיאון against the זיקה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the משנה supports רבי אושעיא. A minor יבמה can refuse the יבם's מאמר, but not the זיקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this supports רבי אושעיא. For רבי אושעיא said: She can refuse his מאמר, but she cannot refuse his זיקה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question with a suggestion. The משנה doesn't let her refuse now because, as רבי אושעיא says, מיאון does not work against the bond of יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the husband dies, all that is left between her and the family is the זיקה, the bond of יבום. מיאון was made only to undo a marriage, so it can undo a מאמר, but not a זיקה. This explains why the משנה does not let her refuse now, so it seems to prove רבי אושעיא right.

keyTerms.meaning: let us say it supports him
a kiddushin the יבם gives the יבמה before יבום, made by the rabbis
the bond of יבום between the יבמה and the יבם

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets out a clear limit on מיאון. It undoes a marriage or a מאמר, but it cannot undo the זיקה of יבום.

phrases.english: Let us say this supports רבי אושעיא.
For רבי אושעיא said:
She can refuse his מאמר,
phrases.notes: "She" is a minor יבמה, and "his" means the יבם's.

phrases.english: but she cannot refuse his זיקה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by suggesting the משנה proves רבי אושעיא's rule
steps.raayaObject: רבי אושעיא's rule that a minor cannot use מיאון against the זיקה
steps.raayaSupportSource: Our משנה, which does not let the minor ערוה do מיאון after the death to free her צרה

steps.title: The rival wife of a forbidden relative is a special case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof for רבי אושעיא. Maybe a minor can refuse the זיקה, but a צרת ערוה is different.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. The rival wife of an ערוה is a different case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from Step 17. It says the משנה doesn't prove that a minor can't refuse the זיקה, because a צרת ערוה follows her own special rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 17 the גמרא thought the משנה shows a minor can't refuse the זיקה. Now it says: maybe she can refuse it, but even so the צרה stays forbidden for a different reason. The next step gives that reason.

keyTerms.meaning: The co-wife of a woman who is forbidden to the יבם
Is different, follows its own rule

phrases.english: No, the rival wife of a forbidden relative is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof for רבי אושעיא offered in Step 17
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof only. It does not say רבי אושעיא is wrong.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה's ruling could come from a special rule about צרת ערוה, not from any limit on מיאון against the זיקה

steps.title: רמי בר יחזקאל's teaching about refusing the husband versus refusing the יבם
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: if a minor refused her husband, she may marry his father. If she refused only the יבם, she is forbidden to his father.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רמי בר יחזקאל taught: if she refused the husband, she is permitted to his father. If she refused the יבם, she is forbidden to his father.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up its claim that a צרת ערוה is different. It compares refusing a husband with refusing a יבם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Refusing the husband cancels the marriage, so she was never his daughter-in-law. Refusing the יבם happens after the husband died, and she is still forbidden to the father. So her מיאון at that stage can't erase everything.

keyTerms.meaning: She refused, meaning she did מיאון and cancelled a marriage made while she was a minor
The brother-in-law who could do יבום

phrases.english: As רמי בר יחזקאל taught:
If she refused the husband, she is permitted to his father.
If she refused the יבם, she is forbidden to his father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind the claim in Step 18
steps.raayaObject: That a צרת ערוה is different and stays forbidden even if the ערוה later refuses

steps.title: Once she falls to יבום, she already looks like a forbidden relative
steps.stepSummary: From the moment of falling to יבום she looks like the father's daughter-in-law. In the same way, the צרה looks like the יבם's daughter's co-wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: So we see: from the moment she fell to יבום, she looks like his daughter-in-law. Here too, from the moment she fell to יבום, she looks like the rival wife of his daughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the lesson from the ברייתא and applies it to our משנה. This closes the answer begun in Step 18.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What matters is how things looked when the husband died and she fell to יבום. At that moment the צרה looked like the co-wife of the יבם's daughter. A later מיאון can't undo that look, so she stays forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: From the moment she fell to יבום, when the husband died

steps.whatToRemember: The status set at the moment of נפילה sticks. A minor's later מיאון can't remove the look of being a צרת ערוה, so the משנה doesn't prove רבי אושעיא's rule.

phrases.english: Apparently:
from the time she fell to יבום, she appears as his daughter-in-law.
Here too:
from the time she fell to יבום, she appears as his daughter's rival wife.
phrases.notes: "His" means the יבם. In the גמרא's example, the minor ערוה is the יבם's own daughter; the משנה's rule covers any minor ערוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the principle out of the ברייתא and applies it to the צרה in our משנה
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A צרת ערוה stays forbidden because of how things looked at the moment of נפילה, even if the ערוה later refuses

steps.title: A new משנה: six stricter עריות whose rival wives are permitted
steps.stepSummary: Six עריות are more severe than those in the first משנה. They can only be married to others, so their צרות are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Six forbidden relatives are more severe than these, because they are married to others. Their rival wives are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It brings up six forbidden women who work differently from the fifteen in the first משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These women could never be married to any of the brothers, so יבום never applies to them at all. Since a צרה is only forbidden when there is a יבום case, these צרות are permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה, the start of a new משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Don't get mixed up: "more severe" here leads to a more lenient result for the צרה. Because these women are forbidden to every brother, יבום never comes up, so their צרות go free.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Six forbidden relatives
are more severe than these,
phrases.notes: "These" means the fifteen women listed in the first משנה of the פרק.

phrases.english: because they are married to others,
their rival wives are permitted:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the previous discussion ended
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Six עריות that can never be married to the brothers do not make their צרות forbidden, because יבום never applies to them

steps.title: The list of the six women
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists the six: mother, father's wife, father's sister, paternal sister, father's brother's wife, and paternal brother's wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: His mother, his father's wife, his father's sister, his sister from his father, the wife of his father's brother, and the wife of his brother from his father.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now names the six women it mentioned in Step 21.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each woman is forbidden to all the brothers equally, because they all share the same father. That is why none of them could ever come to יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: His sister from the same father
The wife of his father's brother, his aunt by marriage

phrases.english: His mother, and his father's wife,
and his father's sister, his sister from his father,
and the wife of his father's brother,
and the wife of his brother from his father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the six women introduced in Step 21
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The six are: mother, father's wife, father's sister, paternal sister, father's brother's wife, and paternal brother's wife

steps.title: בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about the co-wives
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי permit the צרות to marry the brothers through יבום; בית הלל forbid them.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי allow the co-wives to the brothers, and בית הלל forbid them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now tells us that the rule we learned until now, that a צרת ערוה is exempt, is actually a מחלוקת between בית שמאי and בית הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, everything assumed the צרה is exempt from יבום just like the ערוה herself. בית שמאי disagree: they hold the צרה may do יבום with the brothers. בית הלל forbid her, and the earlier משניות follow בית הלל.

keyTerms.meaning: Co-wives: other wives of the same husband

steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי: the צרה of an ערוה may do יבום with the brothers. בית הלל: she may not. The earlier משניות follow בית הלל.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the sides. Here it is בית שמאי who permit (the lenient side about יבום), and בית הלל who forbid.
steps.whyThisMatters: This מחלוקת is a well-known one, and it shows that the whole idea of exempting the צרה, which the earlier steps relied on, is בית הלל's view.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai permit the co-wives to the brothers,
and Beit Hillel forbid them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After listing the six עריות whose צרות are permitted, the משנה now shows that the exemption of צרות in general is a מחלוקת between בית שמאי and בית הלל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: צרות of עריות are permitted to the brothers for יבום. בית הלל: they are forbidden.
